newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt coalition seen solid after meeting.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt coalition seen solid after meeting.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government has emerged from a meeting of coalition party leaders stronger than before, the head of the Popular Party was quoted as saying by Italian newsagency Ansa.
"The situation has been unblocked. There was no break-up. The (governing) majority has become compact again," Franco Marini said as he left the meeting.

The meeting was called to discuss government proposals to boost employment. The plans have created strains in an already tense coalition, with hard-left ally Communist Refoundation threatening to vote down the measures.
Refoundation lies outside the coalition but guarantees its majority in the lower house of parliament.
Some government parties, including the Popular Party, have complained that Refoundation was gaining too much power over decision-making in Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition.
Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti attended Thursday's meeting -- the first time he has been invited to a summit of coalition heads.
The small party objected to government plans to introduce incentives encouraging short term contracts and temporary work schemes. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
